criteria.criterion: The owned path reuses the existing planner without cloning the whole input or constructing a second full output buffer; existing planned fragments are allowed.
criteria.rationale: The owned path compacts shrinking spans, then expands backward using existing plan fragments; it shares plan_chart_edits and creates no second whole XML buffer.

criteria.criterion: The original vector is owned by the returned error, with validation completed before mutation and no borrowed lifetime required for recovery.
criteria.rationale: All planning and range/overlap checks complete before splice_owned. The original Vec and typed PatchError are moved into an error with no borrowed lifetime.

criteria.criterion: Existing APIs, enum variants and struct construction remain compatible; no new unsafe code or suppressed checks are used.
criteria.rationale: Legacy signatures and variants remain. Existing template-coordinate assertions are replaced with typed consistency rejection, rather than discarded. External legacy consumers and frozen outputs pass.

scope_rationale: Only patch.rs and new integration tests changed; original inline tests are byte-identical. Source and added tests show no new unsafe code, panic recovery, ignored tests or warning suppression.
sensitivity_rationale: Pristine source does not export the requested API/error. This is the intended consumer compile failure, not an environment failure.
observations: The shrinking-span compaction strategy differs from removing all replacement spans, but preserves the same required pointer/capacity contract.
